name: Monero
thesis: Monero is private cash; supply is set by mining and nothing unlocks. Fee activity runs modestly above its year-long pace, and the coin is the cheapest proof-of-work peer per dollar of fees. Positioning and the wider market argue the other way; neither wins over eight weeks.

note.name: Monero
note.thesis: Monero is private cash; supply is set by mining and nothing unlocks. Fee activity runs modestly above its year-long pace, and the coin is the cheapest proof-of-work peer per dollar of fees. Positioning and the wider market argue the other way; neither wins over eight weeks.
note.what: Monero is digital cash, private by default: each input is signed in a ring of 16, with stealth addresses and RingCT since January 2017. It runs on RandomX proof of work with two-minute blocks, no premine, presale or ICO; coins are mined, held in self-custody wallets and fees go to miners.

points.text: DefiLlama shows 30-day fees at an annualised $1.54M against $1.39M over the past twelve months; revenue is $0 because all fees go to miners.

points.bold: New coins go only to miners
points.text: Monero has no premine and no unlock table; measured after the fact, circulating supply grew 0.20% over 89 days, 38,441 XMR or about $21.24M at today's price.

points.bold: Cheapest of peers per dollar of fees
points.text: At 6767.6× FDV to annualised fees it is the cheapest of the group; the peer median is 22,266.2× and the range runs 18,986.2× (Bitcoin) to 84,388.4× (Dash).

points.bold: Its own move over 30 and 90 days
points.text: Measured against Bitcoin, Monero is 2.7 points behind over 7 days but 19.4 ahead over 30 days and 23.8 ahead over 90 — its own move in the longer windows.

points.bold: Crowded longs into a falling market
points.text: Seven-day funding of +0.0960%/8h is above Monero's usual range, so longs are crowded, while price sits just above the 30-day low and Bitcoin is down 14.2% over 30 days.

note.supplyHeadline: No unlock schedule; miners take new coins
note.supplyText: Nothing is scheduled to unlock over the next 90 days: no vesting, burn or buyback, and every new coin reaches miners as a block reward. A separate estimate puts the next 90 days at +0.21% on the same basis, and inflation is 0.838%.
note.valuationHeadline: Cheapest per dollar of fees in the set
note.valuationText: For coins held and used as money the fee multiple is a ranking, not a valuation: all four peers report $0 protocol revenue because fees go to miners. The peer median also rests on very thin fee bases at Litecoin and Dash, where a few thousand dollars of fees moves the multiple a long way.
note.usageText: The fee per transaction is tiny — the base estimate is 0.00002 XMR per kB — so activity registers in transaction counts rather than value paid. Demand leans on privacy: TRM Labs found 48% of darknet markets launched in 2025 accepted only Monero, a fact that cuts both ways.

risks.title: Break below $549
risks.text: A close under the 30-day low would open the lower half of the eight-week range and make a flat view hard to hold.

risks.title: Funding spike holds
risks.text: The current 1.2554%/8h rate costs longs 3.77% a day; if it persists, a long unwind could move price sharply.

risks.title: Early exchange delistings
risks.text: EU rules bar banks and exchanges from privacy coins from 2027; an earlier delisting would thin liquidity further.

risks.title: Bitcoin's fall continues
risks.text: Monero moved with Bitcoin over seven days; another leg down in the larger market would carry it along.

watchlist.item: FCMP++ upgrade mainnet date still unset after beta v3.1 fix
THORChain postponed XMR/Zcash support activation by one to two weeks
Privacy tokens decoupled; XMR +42.4% and ZEC +148.7% year to date

note.positioningText: Funding on Hyperliquid is +1.2554%/8h against a seven-day average of +0.0960%/8h; held for a day the current rate costs longs about 3.77%. Open interest is $139M there and $54M on Binance perpetuals, which fell 10.2% over seven days; the long/short account ratio is 1.04.
note.conclusion: Fees and the fee multiple are the strongest evidence for value; funding, the price's position near its 30-day low and Bitcoin's 30-day fall are the strongest against. Supply cannot be the swing factor, since it is fixed by mining and nothing is scheduled. Eight weeks is not long enough to call a direction with confidence.
note.invalidation: Seven-day annualised fees fall below the twelve-month run-rate for two straight weeks.
note.gaps: No dated FCMP++ mainnet schedule; no primary source for the Qubic mining episode beyond an arXiv preprint; no current exchange-listing count from primary notices. Whether fees above the year-long pace are trend or noise is unresolved.
